The *Samādhipañha* ("The Question on Samādhi", Mil 3.1.14) is a text in the *Milindapañha* collection [SuttaCentral]. It is available in modern translation in three languages, including an English translation by John Kelly [SuttaCentral].
A full parallel to the dialogue is preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon as T 1670b 2.13 (*Concentration*) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, the text shares thematic connections or is noted as mentioned in canonical and post-canonical treatises, including the *Cetanākaraṇīyasutta* (AN 11.2), three canonical discourses titled *Samādhisutta* (SN 22.5, SN 35.99, and SN 56.1), the *Paññattihāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 14), and the *Hāravibhaṅgapañcamabhūmi* of the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 5) [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 133 matching passages shared between the *Samādhipañha* and 12 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial textual reuse occurs with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45, where §2.2–2.3 shares text with §141–145.1.1–141–145.1.2 at a similarity of 0.94), the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), and internal parallels across other sections of the *Milindapañha*—including Mil 3.3.5, Mil 3.1.13, Mil 3.2.6, Mil 3.2.3, and Mil 3.4.6 [DharmaNexus]. Other recurring phrasing appears in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), and the *Yamaka* (Ya 1.1.1) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with a score of 10 or greater are detected by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
